title.en: Then and now: if I'd listened

rule.sl:
Takrat in zdaj se lahko mešata. Kar je bilo takrat, kar je zdaj: **if** + **had** + deležnik, **would** + osnovna oblika: **If I'd listened, I'd be there now.** (Če bi takrat {m:poslušal|f:poslušala}, bi bil{m:|f:a} zdaj tam.) Prvi **'d** je had, drugi would.

Kar je vedno, kar je bilo takrat: **if** + preteklik, **would have** + deležnik: **If I knew the way, I wouldn't have got lost.**

**unless** pomeni če ne: **We'll go unless it rains.** En ne je dovolj: **We won't go unless it stops.**

**as long as**, **provided that**, **providing** pomenijo samo če: **You can have the van as long as you bring it back.**

**in case** pove, kaj narediš prej, ker se lahko zgodi: **Take a coat in case it rains.** **if** je drugače: **Take a coat if it rains.** (samo takrat)

Za vsemi je sedanjik, brez will. V govoru ljudje rečejo tudi *If I'd have listened*. Pisno velja **If I had listened**.
rule.de:
Damals und jetzt können sich mischen. Was damals war, was jetzt ist: **if** + **had** + Partizip, **would** + Grundform: **If I'd listened, I'd be there now.** (Hätte ich zugehört, wäre ich jetzt dort.) Das erste **'d** ist had, das zweite would.

Was immer so ist, was damals war: **if** + Vergangenheit, **would have** + Partizip: **If I knew the way, I wouldn't have got lost.**

**unless** heißt wenn nicht: **We'll go unless it rains.** Ein nicht genügt: **We won't go unless it stops.**

**as long as**, **provided that**, **providing** heißen nur wenn: **You can have the van as long as you bring it back.**

**in case** sagt, was du vorher tust, weil es geschehen kann: **Take a coat in case it rains.** **if** ist anders: **Take a coat if it rains.** (nur dann)

Danach das Präsens, kein will. Gesprochen sagt man auch *If I'd have listened*. Geschrieben gilt **If I had listened**.
rule.it:
Allora e adesso si possono mescolare. Ciò che è stato, ciò che è adesso: **if** + **had** + participio, **would** + forma base: **If I'd listened, I'd be there now.** (Se avessi ascoltato, adesso sarei lì.) Il primo **'d** è had, il secondo would.

Ciò che è sempre, ciò che è stato: **if** + il passato, **would have** + participio: **If I knew the way, I wouldn't have got lost.**

**unless** vuol dire se non: **We'll go unless it rains.** Basta un no: **We won't go unless it stops.**

**as long as**, **provided that**, **providing** vogliono dire solo se: **You can have the van as long as you bring it back.**

**in case** dice che cosa fai prima, perché può succedere: **Take a coat in case it rains.** **if** è diverso: **Take a coat if it rains.** (solo allora)

Dopo c'è il presente, niente will. A voce si dice anche *If I'd have listened*. Per iscritto vale **If I had listened**.
rule.en:
Then and now can mix. What happened then, what is so now: **if** + **had** + the participle, **would** + the base form: **If I'd listened, I'd be there now.** The first **'d** is had, the second would.

What is always so, what happened then: **if** + the past, **would have** + the participle: **If I knew the way, I wouldn't have got lost.**

**unless** means if not: **We'll go unless it rains.** One not is enough: **We won't go unless it stops.**

**as long as**, **provided that**, **providing** mean only if: **You can have the van as long as you bring it back.**

**in case** says what you do first, because it may happen: **Take a coat in case it rains.** **if** is different: **Take a coat if it rains.** (only then)

After all of them, the present, no will. In talk people also say *If I'd have listened*. Writing wants **If I had listened**.

title.sl: If I'd listened, I'd be there now
title.de: If I'd listened, I'd be there now
title.it: If I'd listened, I'd be there now
title.en: If I'd listened, I'd be there now

rule.sl: Takrat, zato zdaj: **If I'd listened, I'd be there now.** Vedno, zato takrat: **If I knew the way, I wouldn't have got lost.** **unless**: če ne. **as long as**, **provided that**: samo če. **in case**: za vsak primer. Za njimi sedanjik, brez will.
rule.de: Damals, darum jetzt: **If I'd listened, I'd be there now.** Immer, darum damals: **If I knew the way, I wouldn't have got lost.** **unless**: wenn nicht. **as long as**, **provided that**: nur wenn. **in case**: für den Fall. Danach das Präsens, kein will.
rule.it: Allora, perciò adesso: **If I'd listened, I'd be there now.** Sempre, perciò allora: **If I knew the way, I wouldn't have got lost.** **unless**: se non. **as long as**, **provided that**: solo se. **in case**: nel caso. Dopo il presente, niente will.
rule.en: Then, so now: **If I'd listened, I'd be there now.** Always, so then: **If I knew the way, I wouldn't have got lost.** **unless**: if not. **as long as**, **provided that**: only if. **in case**: because it may happen. After them, the present, no will.

examples.en: If we'd left early, we'd be home by now.
examples.sl: Če bi šli zgodaj, bi bili zdaj že doma.
examples.de: Wären wir früh gegangen, wären wir jetzt schon daheim.
examples.it: Se fossimo partiti presto, adesso saremmo già a casa.

examples.en: Take some bread in case Jack is hungry.
examples.sl: Vzemi kruha, za primer da bo Jack lačen.
examples.de: Nimm Brot mit, falls Jack hungrig ist.
examples.it: Prendi del pane, nel caso Jack abbia fame.

tip.sl: 💡 *Za primer, da bo deževalo* je **in case it rains**: sedanjik, brez will.
tip.de: 💡 *Falls* ist oft **if**; wenn du es vorher tust, weil es geschehen kann: **in case**.
tip.it: 💡 *Nel caso piova* è **in case it rains**: il presente, niente will.
tip.en: 💡 **in case**: do it now, because it may happen. **if**: do it only then.
